subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw provide a supported cross-machine browser relay/extension bridge for managed-hosting users, or keep the legacy extension relay retired and require node-host or remote-CDP based alternatives?
rationale: The request is both a product strategy choice and a browser-control security boundary; automation cannot safely decide whether to restore, replace, or permanently retire this capability.

options.title: Design secure replacement bridge
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend or node-anchored extension bridge with scoped authority, operator consent, auditability, migration behavior, and Plugin SDK/docs coverage.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Close the legacy path intentionally and document the supported managed-hosting alternatives and their limitations for non-technical users.

options.title: Defer to broader backend API
options.body: Keep this issue open while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19289 and the My Browser PRs settle the minimum safe browser-driver contract.

recommendation.title: Design secure replacement bridge
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend or node-anchored extension bridge with scoped authority, operator consent, auditability, migration behavior, and Plugin SDK/docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest direct history on the extension-path removal and existing-session migration surface.
